audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Hwei's CC palette as 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' in eight places — winCon, enemyWin, loading, focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[2].d and three report fields. No such ability exists.
audit.why: Hwei's E is Subject: Torment, which swaps his palette to Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw. 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' is a placeholder that was never replaced, and the packet independently flags that the page 'never names any of Hwei's abilities'. A reader cannot track a cooldown for an ability that is not in the game.
audit.corrected: Every instance re-pointed to Subject: Torment (E), with the three real CC spells named and the palette's 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 cooldown given.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer twice calls Severing Bolt a fear — spikes[3].text ('Severing Bolt fear') and the 'late' paragraph ('Charm vs Severing Bolt fear') — and wants.you[2] tells the reader to dodge it as one.
audit.why: Severing Bolt is on the Subject: Disaster (Q) palette, alongside Devastating Fire and Molten Fissure — those are his damage spells. The fear is Grim Visage, on the Subject: Torment (E) palette. The advice sends the reader to respect the wrong cast on the wrong palette with the wrong cooldown attached.
audit.corrected: Fear re-attributed to Grim Visage; zone control re-attributed to Molten Fissure rather than Devastating Fire.
sources: brief.enemyKit Q text (Devastating Fire, Severing Bolt, Molten Fissure) and E text (Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] reads 'Zone with Passive canvases to control neutral objectives'. Hwei has no canvas passive.
audit.why: Signature of the Visionary primes an enemy champion on the first damaging spell and completes on the second, leaving a signature beneath them that detonates after a short delay. It is a burst-completion mechanic, not zone control — and it dictates the actual laning rule, which is never to eat two spells in a row.
audit.corrected: 'Complete his signature by hitting you with two spells', with the matching player-side rule written into tradeGood.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].side and phases[5].side read 'Skill' while win[4] and win[5] read 'Ahri'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart agrees with the content layer (Skill x4, Ahri, Ahri, Skill), so the full layer is the outlier on the two rows where Ahri's ultimate actually changes the lane.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side and phases[5].side -> Ahri. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty is stated as EVEN with the reason 'out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time' — no mechanic named.
audit.why: The real shape of the lane is that Hwei has three separate palette cooldowns (Q 10/9/8/7/6, W 18-16, E 12-10) and no mobility whatsoever, so the lane is decided by which palette he is holding when Ahri steps up — not by raw range.
audit.corrected: Difficulty re-grounded on the Subject: Torment cooldown and on Hwei having no dash.
sources: brief.enemyKit cooldowns; no dash flag on any Hwei ability

audit.whatIsWrong: Subject: Serenity is never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: It is his shield/heal/speed palette on an 18-second rank-1 cooldown, and the missingInteractions entry flags it as absorbing Ahri's burst window. Committing a full charm combo into a fresh Serenity is the single most common way this lane is thrown, and nothing warns the reader.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, breakdown.trading and dontsFull[0].d — force it out before you commit.

notes: The packet defect 'never names any of Hwei's abilities' was accurate and is now fixed: the page invented an ability called 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' and used it in eight places as the matchup's tracked cooldown. The real CC palette is Subject: Torment (E), holding Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw. A second, separate error ran through the content layer: Severing Bolt was described as a fear in two places, but it is a Subject: Disaster (Q) damage spell — the fear is Grim Visage. Both are corrected. The packet suspectName on whys[4] ('Spirit Rush's') is a FALSE POSITIVE — that is Ahri's own R and the line is left alone. One thing I deliberately did not write: Riot's kit text does not spell out what Crushing Maw actually does (the E-palette entry only lists the three spell names), so I named it without asserting an effect. Same for the individual Subject: Serenity spells — I wrote the shield generically rather than attributing it to Stirring Lights or Pool of Reflection, since the text does not say which grants what.
